goal: Resolve the four unconsumed Pmcro__* env vars AppHost passes to Runtime/OrchestrationApi with real evidence: wire them to an actual consumer if one exists or is documented, otherwise remove them as dead configuration.

steps.action: Grep ProjectName.Runtime, ProjectName.OrchestrationApi, and ProjectName.ServiceDefaults for any reference to Pmcro or the four specific variable names, and check whether any design doc (CONTEXT.md, AGENTS.md, .pmcro/HANDOFF.md, .pmcro/runtime/*) ties the .NET services to the separate .pmcro/runtime PowerShell engine.
Based on the evidence, decide: wire the vars up (if a real consumer or documented intent exists) or remove them from AppHost.cs (if they are unconsumed dead configuration). Execute that decision.
Confirm dotnet build ProjectName.slnx succeeds with 0 errors after the change, and that the decision is backed by the grep/doc evidence rather than assumption.

Commit and push. If removing, file a next_seed only if there is a real, evidenced case for a future properly-scoped design cycle to give the Runtime agent live PMCR-O awareness -- do not silently invent the feature here.

success_criteria: Decision (wire vs remove) is backed by a real grep across all three .NET projects plus a check of the design docs, not assumption
If removed: AppHost.cs no longer passes the four Pmcro__* env vars, and dotnet build still succeeds
If wired: at least one Program.cs actually reads and uses the value, and dotnet build still succeeds
dotnet build ProjectName.slnx succeeds with 0 errors after the change
Change committed and pushed to origin
out_of_scope: Designing or building live PMCR-O tool access for the Runtime chat agent -- if evidence supports doing this eventually, it gets its own properly-scoped next_seed, not silent implementation here
Any change to the separate .pmcro/runtime PowerShell deterministic engine itself
name_rationale: Names exactly what this cycle does: resolves whether the Pmcro env vars are wired up or removed.
